newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Novosibirskenergo to ask AGM to increase capital.
newsitem.headline: Novosibirskenergo to ask AGM to increase capital.

text.p: Russian regional energy company Novosibirskenergo will ask shareholders to vote on an increase in charter capital to 128.6 billion roubles at a June 16 general meeting, a spokesman said.

Dmitry Zhurba, deputy executive director of Novosibirskenergo's financial consultants Soyuz Energoservis Association, said the eight-fold increase in capital would be effected by revaluing company assets.
"The increase in charter capital to 128.6 billion roubles is planned through a further share issue. That way each shareholder will receive seven shares for every one he already holds," said Zhurba.

He said Nobosibirskenergo board of directors confirmed a previous increase in charter capital from 15.08 billion roubles to 16.08 billion roubles. He said details of the share issue had been sent to the Ministry of Finance for registration.
Novosibirskenergo press secretary Vadim Matveyev told Reuters that the board had decided to call the annual general meeting on June 16. Earlier reports said the meeting would be held on May 17.

According to previously announced plans, shareholders will vote on dividends of 600 roubles on ordinary shares and 1,400 roubles on preferred shares, both with a face value of 1,000 roubles, at the AGM.
Dividends in 1995 were 500 roubles and 3,000 roubles on ordinary and preferred shares respectively.

Zhurba said Novosibirskenergo's biggest shareholders included Novosibirsk administration with 20 percent of shares, national power company UES with 12 percent, and Russia's IFK Alemar with 29 percent.
